2610.06748.title: BazaarBench: Delegation Safety in Decentralized C2C Marketplaces Run by LLM Agents
2610.06748.paper_summary: In decentralized consumer-to-consumer (C2C) marketplaces, people list goods, negotiate with strangers, and rate one another, so trust rests on reputation. Large language model (LLM) agents now act for users, raising risks to their money, privacy, and reputation. We introduce BazaarBench, a simulated C2C marketplace and benchmark for evaluating the safety of these agents. It tracks ownership, item condition, and commitments across transactions, combining record checks with rubric-based LLM judgments to identify six failure types across five stages. We run three base markets for 30 simulated days, each with 100 agents using one model and inventories drawn from a public eBay sample. Across 45 continuations, we evaluate five models under ordinary instructions, deadline pressure, or adversarial instructions to exploit other traders. Each continuation runs for seven simulated days from a copy of a market's day-30 state. The tested model controls the same 20 selected agents, retaining their personas, inventories, and histories, while the other 80 keep the base model. All five models attempt to promise the same item to multiple buyers under ordinary instructions. Adding targets and deadlines increases these attempts for every model. Under adversarial instructions, the share of tested sellers' committed transactions completed despite unavailable items or overstated conditions rises from 15.4% to 33.4%, reaching 55.5% for GPT-5.4. Averaged across models and markets, simulated weekly earnings per tested agent rise from USD 20 under ordinary instructions to USD 33 under adversarial instructions. Most of the increase comes from items the sellers never held. We release the simulator, saved market states, evaluation code, and records covering 357,608 agent model calls for evaluating new models and developing safer marketplace agents.
2610.06748.paper_summary_zh: 在去中心化的消費者對消費者 (C2C) 市場中，人們列出商品、與陌生人協商並互相評價，因此信任建立在聲譽之上。大型語言模型 (LLM) 代理現在為用戶行事，這提高了他們的金錢、隱私和聲譽的風險。我們介紹了 BazaarBench，一個模擬的 C2C 市場和用於評估這些代理安全性的基準。它追蹤交易中的所有權、物品狀況和承諾，結合記錄檢查與基於標準的 LLM 判斷，以識別五個階段中的六種失敗類型。我們運行三個基礎市場，模擬 30 天，每個市場有 100 名代理使用一個模型，並從公共 eBay 樣本中提取庫存。在 45 次延續中，我們在普通指令、截止日期壓力或對抗性指令下評估五個模型，以利用其他交易者。每次延續從市場的第 30 天狀態的副本運行七天模擬。測試的模型控制相同的 20 名選定代理，保留他們的個性、庫存和歷史，而其他 80 名則保持基礎模型。所有五個模型在普通指令下嘗試向多個買家承諾相同的商品。增加目標和截止日期會增加每個模型的這些嘗試。在對抗性指令下，測試的賣家承諾的交易在物品不可用或狀況誇大下完成的比例從 15.4% 上升到 33.4%，對於 GPT-5.4 則達到 55.5%。在模型和市場之間平均，測試代理的模擬每週收入從普通指令下的 20 美元上升到對抗性指令下的 33 美元。大部分增長來自賣家從未持有的物品。我們釋放了模擬器、保存的市場狀態、評估代碼以及涵蓋 357,608 次代理模型調用的記錄，以評估新模型並開發更安全的市場代理。
